chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Nadr ibn Shuayb, from Khalid ibn Mad al-Qalanisi, from al-Qindi, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, is everyone who says "there is no god but God" a believer? He said: Indeed, enmity towards us follows the Jews and the Christians. Surely, you will not enter Paradise until you love me, and he who claims that he loves me while hating this one — meaning Ali (peace be upon him) — has lied.

key_terms.الجنة: Paradise — the eternal abode promised to the faithful
key_terms.عداوة: Enmity, hostility — opposition toward the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.مؤمن: Believer — one with true faith, not merely verbal testimony
key_terms.يبغض: To hate, to bear malice — opposite of the love required for true faith

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about loving Ali and entering Paradise?
ai.summary: In this hadith transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) from his forefathers, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) responds to a man's question about whether the mere utterance of the shahada makes one a believer. The Prophet declares that hostility toward the Ahl al-Bayt is akin to the enmity of the Jews and Christians, and that entry into Paradise requires love for the Prophet and Ali (AS). This teaching underscored for the early Muslim community that faith is not merely a verbal declaration but must include loyalty to the Prophet's designated successors.
